canvas-01-1.description: The first sheet of the atlas carries the title, the key map, the water and fire department report, the legend and the street and specials index in its upper half; this part is the map in the lower left, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It covers the east side of Butler from William Street on the west to just beyond Fairview Avenue on the east, between High Street at the top and Cary Avenue at the bottom. George Street and Ward Avenue run north to south between High Street and Cary Avenue, Central Avenue and Van Buren Street cross between them, and Minton Avenue and Wood Avenue are drawn but marked not open. Myrtle Avenue leaves Cary Avenue southward at the bottom. The district is thinly built: frame dwellings with sheds and garages stand along High Street, William Street, George Street and Cary Avenue, while the large blocks between Ward Avenue and Fairview Avenue are almost empty, with a single large dwelling in the middle. Water pipes are drawn in High Street, Ward Avenue, Central Avenue and Cary Avenue, with hydrants and a fire alarm box. The top and east margins are marked no exposure beyond, and a heavy line on the right separates the second part of the sheet. The large compass rose and the scale bar of the sheet stand in this part.
notes: Cary Avenue is Carey Avenue today; Ward is Ward Avenue and Van Buren is Van Buren Street.
Minton Avenue and Wood Avenue are marked not open; neither is a named street in OpenStreetMap today.
The upper half of the sheet (title, index, key map of the borough at 1,340 feet to an inch, water facilities and fire department notes) is outside this part.

Sheet 1: title, key map (1,340 ft to an inch), water and fire notes, legend and street index in the upper half; below, two map parts at 100 ft: part 1 (High Street to Cary Avenue, William Street to Fairview Avenue) and part 2 right of a heavy line (Myrtle Avenue between Cary and Belleview Avenues). Part 2 has only three junctions (exact fit).

canvas-01-2.description: The second part of the first sheet lies to the right of a heavy line below the index, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and at the same angle as the main part. It shows Myrtle Avenue running from Cary Avenue south-westward to Belleview Avenue, with the end of George Street entering Cary Avenue at the top. The lots on both sides of Myrtle Avenue hold frame dwellings with outbuildings and a few concrete block garages; the large blocks either side are partly vacant. A water pipe runs in Cary Avenue, Myrtle Avenue and Belleview Avenue, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at Myrtle Avenue. A note on Belleview Avenue gives 350 feet to a two-storey frame dwelling beyond, and the margins are marked no exposure beyond. The scale bar of the sheet is drawn at the foot of the dividing line.
notes: Cary Avenue is Carey Avenue today.

Only three junctions are drawn (Cary Avenue at George Street and Myrtle Avenue, Belleview Avenue at Myrtle Avenue), so the fit passes exactly through them; George Street at Cary Avenue was hand-picked.

Sheet 1: title, key map (1,340 ft to an inch), water and fire notes, legend and street index in the upper half; below, two map parts at 100 ft: part 1 (High Street to Cary Avenue, William Street to Fairview Avenue) and part 2 right of a heavy line (Myrtle Avenue between Cary and Belleview Avenues). Part 2 has only three junctions (exact fit).

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the north end of Butler's Main Street and the ground between it and the Pequannock River, from the steel bridge at the top left down to Manning Avenue at the bottom, and east to 3rd Street. Main Street runs down the west side lined with dwellings and a few businesses: a garage and auto repair shop, the Park Hotel with stores beside it, and a photographer's shop near Manning Avenue. Laurel Street runs east from Main Street at the top to the works of the Pequannock Rubber Company, whose settling basins and race lie along the river; the rubber reclaiming plant itself stands south of them, between Main Street and West Arch Street, and the company's report is referred to sheet 9. West Arch Street runs north-east from Manning Avenue and then turns east to 3rd Street, with frame dwellings on both sides; the Baptist Church stands on the block between West Arch Street, Manning Avenue and 3rd Street. The river forms the county and borough line, Butler in Morris County on this side and Bloomingdale in Passaic County beyond, and the sheet notes See Map of Bloomingdale. An inset at the upper right shows a saw mill on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike about a mile and a half north-west of the post office. Water pipes are drawn in Main Street, West Arch Street and Manning Avenue.
notes: West Arch Street is part of Arch Street today; Laurel is Laurel Street.
The Pequannock Rubber Co. buildings here are cross-referenced to sheet 9 for their report.
The inset at the upper right (Leo Lust saw mill on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike, 1.5 miles north-west of the post office) was not georeferenced: it shows no street junction.

50 ft. Part 1: Main Street north of Manning Avenue, Laurel Street, West Arch Street to 3rd Street, Pequannock Rubber Co. settling basins. Part 2: inset at upper right, Leo Lust saw mill on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike 1.5 miles NW of the post office; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Leo Lust saw mill on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike, 1.5 miles north-west of the post office (no street junction (only the turnpike and the abandoned railroad branch are drawn); needs hand-picked control (parcel corners or a surviving road feature near the Pequannock River crossing)).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the centre of Butler at 50 feet to an inch: the curving business stretch of Main Street from Manning Avenue at the top left down to the railroad, and the land east of it up to 3rd Street. The west side of Main Street is lined with brick and frame stores, many with dwellings or halls above, a movie house (vacant), drug stores, an automobile store and a hall; behind them the ground rises, and one block is built into the hillside. East of Main Street lies the large Butler Cemetery, with house lots along Manning Avenue, Plain Street and 3rd Street around it; Plain Street continues east of 3rd Street as a street not yet opened. A short street marked Cemetery runs from Plain Street down to Main Street, where a group of brick stores stands at the corner. The Erie Railroad (New York, Susquehanna and Western branch, main line) crosses the lower part of the sheet beside Main Street, and below it Kikeout Brook flows through Coxs Pond, with a dam, past Park Place and High Street. At the bottom left Park Place, Kiel Avenue and Boonton Avenue meet at a concrete bridge over the brook, and the Fire Department and Borough Hall building stands on Park Place near High Street, with dwellings along High Street and Roberts Street. Stores and warehouses of other sheets are sketched at the lower right. Water pipes run in Main Street, Manning Avenue, Plain Street, Park Place and High Street.
notes: Plain Street is Plane Street today; the street marked Cemetery is today's Short Street; Roberts Street is Robert Street.
Plain Street east of 3rd Street is marked not opened.
Few junctions survive on this sheet and most lie along Main Street, so its own fit is weak (leave-one-out about 30 m in the first pass).

50 ft. Main Street business district from Manning Avenue to the railroad, Butler Cemetery, Plain Street (Plane Street), Cemetery (Short Street), Park Place, Coxs Pond, Borough Hall. Few junctions; weak first-pass fit.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the east end of Butler's business district between Manning Avenue at the top and the railroad, from 3rd Street on the west to the Pequannock River, which forms the line with Bloomingdale and Passaic County on the east. Main Street crosses the lower part of the sheet and leaves it over a concrete bridge across the river; 2nd Street (not opened north of the block) and East Arch Street run up from Main Street to Manning Avenue, itself marked not opened, and Plain Street, also not opened, meets 3rd Street at the left. The blocks along Main Street and East Arch Street hold the commercial buildings: The Butler movie theatre with stage and balcony, stores with halls above, a plumber, a drug store, a paint shop, the Butler Argus printing office and dwellings behind; the upper blocks are mostly open lots with a few houses and hen houses. South of Main Street, Kikeout Brook runs past stores and dwellings to the river, with the Butler Coal and Lumber Company's sheds, coal pockets and trestle on the left and the Bloomingdale Rubber Company's rubber reclaiming works, its grinding and cleaning buildings and a pond on the right. The Erie Railroad (New York, Susquehanna and Western branch) crosses below, and Rodda Street enters at the bottom of the sheet. Water pipes run in Main Street, East Arch Street and Manning Avenue.
notes: East Arch is part of Arch Street today; Plain is Plane Street.
Manning Avenue, Plain Street and 2nd Street north of the block are marked not opened.

All three control points were hand-picked (3rd Street and Manning Avenue, 2nd Street and Manning Avenue, East Arch and Main Street); the detector paired building and lot lines at these junctions. The fitted scale agrees with the atlas's other 50-foot sheets.

50 ft. Manning Avenue to the railroad, 3rd Street to the Pequannock River: Main Street, 2nd Street, East Arch, The Butler theatre, Butler Coal & Lumber, Bloomingdale Rubber Co. Placed from three hand-picked junctions.

sheet-5-1.description: The upper half of sheet 5, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the residential blocks east of Butler's centre between the Erie Railroad and High Street. Rodda Street runs east along the top of the built blocks and turns south to meet High Street in the middle of the sheet; High Street crosses the bottom from west to east, with John Street and William Street leaving it southward to the dividing line. Along High Street stand frame dwellings with outbuildings on deep lots, and St. Paul's Episcopal Church; behind them several large lots are vacant or hold only sheds and garages. At the top left, beside Main Street, the Erie Railroad (New York, Susquehanna and Western branch) crosses Kikeout Brook, and Cox's Pond with its dam and island lies below it; the H. W. Smith feed and grain warehouse stands next to the tracks, with a vacant concrete building and another warehouse nearby. Water pipes are drawn in High Street with hydrants and a fire alarm box. A heavy line across the middle of the sheet separates this part from the Riverdale part below.
notes: The upper, east-west stretch of Rodda is Ogden Terrace today; the north-south stretch is Rodda Street.
John Street and William Street are drawn only from High Street to the dividing line; their junctions with High Street were hand-picked.
The fitted scale is about 5 percent smaller than the atlas's 50-foot sheets.

50 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line. Part 1 (upper): Rodda Street (upper stretch now Ogden Terrace) and High Street, Coxs Pond. Part 2 (lower): Riverdale, Main Street on the south bank of the Pequannock with the Erie Railroad, Lissberger & Co. plant, Gulf Refining; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Riverdale: Main Street along the south bank of the Pequannock River, Acton Court (arbitrary), Lissberger & Co. experimental plant, Gulf Refining Co. (no surviving street junction: today's Main Street east of the Turnpike lies north of the river in Bloomingdale (parcels 1601), and no named street follows the drawn Riverdale Main Street; the drawn railroad does not match the modern line well enough to anchor on; needs parcel-corner or carried control along the south bank, after identifying the old Main Street line on the ground).

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the residential south side of central Butler between High Street at the top and Maby Lane at the bottom, from Boonton Avenue and Kikeout Brook on the west to William Street on the east. Kiel Avenue and Park Place meet Boonton Avenue and High Street at the top left, beside the brook. Central Avenue, Cary Avenue and Belleview Avenue cross the sheet from west to east, and Roberts Street, John Street, Bartholdi Avenue and Pearl Place run north to south; Hasbrouck Avenue links Boonton Avenue and Bartholdi Avenue further south, and Cook Street is drawn but marked not opened. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings and outbuildings, more closely built in the north and with large open lots in the middle and south, where a pond lies south of Cary Avenue. Institutions are prominent: the Butler Public School on Bartholdi Avenue, a Methodist Episcopal church between Cary and Belleview Avenues, and St. Anthony's Roman Catholic monastery, school and church on the block between Hasbrouck Avenue and Maby Lane. The Borough of Butler electric plant stands beside Kikeout Brook off Boonton Avenue, with Summit Avenue and Brook Street leaving the sheet on the west. A hall and a paint shop are among the few other non-residential buildings. Water pipes run in most streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. A heavy line at the lower right separates the second part of the sheet, and the margin notes widely scattered dwellings beyond to the south-east.
notes: Cary Avenue is Carey Avenue today, Maby Lane is Mabey Lane and Roberts is Robert Street.
Summit Avenue at the west edge is West Belleview Avenue today.
Cook is marked not opened; today's Cook Street lies about 15 m east of the drawn line.
Like the rest of the atlas, the fit leaves residuals of 2 to 8 m with no single street responsible.

100 ft. Part 1: High Street to Maby Lane, Boonton Avenue to William Street (Butler Public School, St. Anthony's monastery, ME church, electric plant). Part 2 (lower right, heavy line): Boonton and Bartholdi Avenues south of Maby Lane, Washington Street, Cotter and Lafayette Avenues, RC cemetery.

sheet-6-2.description: The second part of sheet 6, set off by a heavy line in the lower right corner of the sheet and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, continues the map south of Maby Lane. It shows Boonton Avenue running south from its junction with Valley Road and Maby Lane, and Bartholdi Avenue parallel to it on the east, with Washington Street, Cotter Avenue and Lafayette Avenue crossing between and beyond them. The blocks are laid out in long narrow house lots, most built with frame dwellings, many with small outbuildings; a convent stands on Maby Lane, and the Bartholdi Hose Company No. 2 fire house on Bartholdi Avenue at Washington Street. The Roman Catholic cemetery occupies the ground east of Bartholdi Avenue, reached by a lane marked Entrance. The streets carry water pipes with hydrants and a fire alarm box. Its own north arrow is drawn at nearly the same angle as the main part. The western edge along the dividing line is marked no exposure beyond, and the bottom margin notes scattered dwellings beyond.
notes: Maby Lane is Mabey Lane today; Washington is Washington Street.
Maby Lane between Boonton Avenue and Bartholdi Avenue is drawn both here and at the foot of the main part of the sheet.
Boonton Avenue at Valley Road and Maby Lane was hand-picked; the other points are along Bartholdi Avenue.

100 ft. Part 1: High Street to Maby Lane, Boonton Avenue to William Street (Butler Public School, St. Anthony's monastery, ME church, electric plant). Part 2 (lower right, heavy line): Boonton and Bartholdi Avenues south of Maby Lane, Washington Street, Cotter and Lafayette Avenues, RC cemetery.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the residential district of Butler west of Boonton Avenue and south of Kiel Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Kiel Avenue runs along the top edge from Oak Street and Spring Street east to the five-way corner with Park Place, High Street and Boonton Avenue; Boonton Avenue curves down the east side past Cary Avenue, Hasbrouck Avenue and Maby Lane, with Kikeout Brook running beside it. Inside, the sheet shows a grid of irregular blocks laid out on rising ground: South Gifford Street running south from Kiel Avenue, Summit Avenue in two offset stretches, Terrace Avenue, Spring Street along the west side with Orchard Street and Smith Street, Elm Avenue running diagonally from Terrace Avenue to Boonton Avenue, Cedar, Beech, Poplar, Brook and Scott Streets, and Valley Road with Alton Place across the south. Center Street appears in the lower left as a street of narrow lots with few houses. The district is almost entirely frame dwellings with outbuildings, many lots still vacant and several large unsubdivided tracts in the south and west. The commercial buildings are at the north-east corner near Park Place: stores, a hall, the post office and the American Legion club rooms on Kiel Avenue. A Church of God stands on Summit Avenue and a wood working shop near Valley Road. Water pipes are drawn in Kiel Avenue, Elm Avenue, Valley Road and Boonton Avenue, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The margins note scattered dwellings beyond to the west and south.
notes: Summit Avenue east of South Gifford is West Belleview Avenue today; Terrace Avenue and the lower stretch of Summit Avenue west of Gifford follow today's Hillside Avenue.

Elm Avenue, Cedar, Beech, Poplar, Brook and Scott are Elm Street, Cedar Street, Beech Street, Poplar Street, Brook Street and Scott Street today; Cary Avenue is Carey Avenue and Maby Lane is Mabey Lane.
Alton Place is marked arbitrary (a name given by the map maker).
Cook Street is marked not opened.
The fit leaves residuals of 4 to 8 m spread over the whole sheet with no single street responsible; the sheet appears to be drawn loosely.

100 ft. Pilot sheet. West of Boonton Avenue south of Kiel Avenue: Gifford, Summit (West Belleview / Hillside), Terrace (Hillside), Elm, Cedar, Beech, Poplar, Brook, Scott, Valley Road, Alton Place, Center Street. Residuals 4-8 m spread over the sheet.

sheet-8-1.description: The main part of sheet 8, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-west residential district of Butler on both sides of Kiel Avenue, which crosses the sheet diagonally from the west edge to Oak Street and Spring Street at the upper right. North of Kiel Avenue, Western Avenue and Fairview Avenue enclose a large block of new house lots (with a group of new houses), and New (White) Street and Oak Street run up towards a road along the top of the built area, below the Pequannock River and its race, which form the Butler and Bloomingdale line (Morris and Passaic Counties). South of Kiel Avenue, Western Avenue continues south past the bottom of the sheet, and Homestead Avenue, Roosevelt Avenue, Orchard Street, Smith Street and Spring Street lay out a grid of long lots. Nearly all buildings are frame dwellings with garages and sheds, thinly scattered; large tracts in the west and south are undivided, and a group of dwellings at the left edge is noted as fronting on Summit Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in Kiel Avenue, Western Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at Kiel and Western Avenues. Two insets in the upper left corner show the upper and lower White Mills of the Pequannock Valley Paper Co. on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike; they are separate parts of the sheet. The bottom margin notes scattered dwellings beyond.
notes: Western Avenue north of Kiel Avenue and both stretches of Fairview Avenue on this sheet form today's North Western Avenue; Western Avenue south of Kiel Avenue keeps its name.
New (White) is New Street today.
The insets of the Pequannock Valley Paper Co. White Mills (upper and lower) were not georeferenced: they show the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike but no street junction.

100 ft. Part 1: north-west district along Kiel Avenue, Western Avenue, Fairview Avenue (both now North Western Avenue), New (White) Street, Roosevelt, Homestead, Orchard, Smith, Spring. Parts 2 and 3: insets of the Pequannock Valley Paper Co. White Mill (upper) and White Mill (lower) on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Pequannock Valley Paper Co., White Mill (upper), on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike (no street junction; needs hand-picked control (parcel corners, river bridge)).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Pequannock Valley Paper Co., White Mill (lower), on the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike near Echo Lake Road (no street junction inside the inset (Echo Lake Road, today Macopin Road, meets the turnpike just below its edge); needs anchor on Macopin Road / Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike extended from the drawn stubs, with px_per_ft and north_deg; low confidence).

sheet-9-1.description: The main part of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers Butler's industrial core along the railroad, between the Pequannock River on the west and Kiel Avenue along the bottom edge. Main Street runs diagonally from the steel bridge over the river at the top left, where Elizabeth Street and the Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike come in from Bloomingdale, down past Laurel Street and Manning Avenue to Park Place at the lower right. Between Main Street and the river stands the large rubber reclaiming plant of the Pequannock Rubber Co., with its numbered buildings, warehouses and piles of rubber and tires. Below it the yard of the New York, Susquehanna and Western (Erie) Railroad fills the middle of the sheet, with a turntable, sidings and the passenger and freight station beside Main Street. South of the tracks the American Hard Rubber Co. works, mutual risk with admittance and plans refused, occupies the block between the railroad, Maple Court and Park Place, and a large open tract of the Pequannock Rubber Co. lies west of Tank Street. Along Kiel Avenue at the bottom, and up Oak Street, Gifford Street and Maple Court, are rows of frame dwellings. Boonton Avenue and High Street meet Park Place at the lower right corner. Fire protection notes describe the two rubber works' watchmen, sprinklers, pumps and water supply. The upper part of the sheet holds two separate parts set off by heavy lines.
notes: Tank is Whitteck Street today.
Kiel Avenue runs along the bottom edge of the sheet; its junctions with Tank and Maple Court and Main Street at Laurel Street were hand-picked.
The railroad yard has been reduced since; the drawn station and yard tracks do not match today's single main line.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Main Street from the steel bridge to Park Place, Pequannock Rubber Co., NYS&W (Erie) yard and station, American Hard Rubber Co., Kiel Avenue along the bottom edge. Part 2 (top left strip): Pequannock Coal & Lumber Co. and Superior Hard Rubber Co. along the river and railroad branch; not placed. Part 3 (upper right): West/East Arch Street, 2nd and 3rd Streets to Manning Avenue.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip at top left: Pequannock Coal & Lumber Co. and Superior Hard Rubber Co. between the Pequannock River and the railroad branch (no street junction (only the river and the abandoned branch line are drawn); needs hand-picked control from the river bank or the branch line (Pompton Industrial Track / Highlands Rail Trail)).

sheet-9-3.description: The upper right part of sheet 9, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the north-east corner of Butler between the Pequannock River and Manning Avenue. West Arch Street runs east along the top of the built area and bends south as East Arch Street at the right, and 3rd Street and 2nd Street run south from it to Manning Avenue at the bottom. The two blocks between 3rd Street, 2nd Street and East Arch Street are laid out in narrow house lots but almost entirely vacant; 2nd Street north of Manning Avenue and Manning Avenue east of it are marked not opened. A row of frame dwellings lines the north side of West Arch Street and the east side of East Arch Street. The river along the top is the Butler and Bloomingdale line between Morris and Passaic Counties, and the sheet notes See Map of Bloomingdale. The part has its own north arrow, drawn at a different angle from the main map, and repeats at a smaller scale the ground of sheets 2 and 4.
notes: West Arch and East Arch are both Arch Street today.
2nd Street and Manning Avenue east of 2nd Street are marked not opened.
2nd Street at Manning Avenue and at West Arch were hand-picked; the four points disagree by about 4 m, as elsewhere in the atlas.

100 ft. Part 1 (main): Main Street from the steel bridge to Park Place, Pequannock Rubber Co., NYS&W (Erie) yard and station, American Hard Rubber Co., Kiel Avenue along the bottom edge. Part 2 (top left strip): Pequannock Coal & Lumber Co. and Superior Hard Rubber Co. along the river and railroad branch; not placed. Part 3 (upper right): West/East Arch Street, 2nd and 3rd Streets to Manning Avenue.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip at top left: Pequannock Coal & Lumber Co. and Superior Hard Rubber Co. between the Pequannock River and the railroad branch (no street junction (only the river and the abandoned branch line are drawn); needs hand-picked control from the river bank or the branch line (Pompton Industrial Track / Highlands Rail Trail)).
